notes.summary: JessQL Hyperscale: multi-table transactional storage, supervised writer services, fair admission, bounded query execution, scalable cold storage, and extensively hardened crash recovery. A major expansion of JessQL's native, strictly typed Luau database architecture.
added: Multi-table managed catalogs with atomic cross-table transactions, shared WAL epochs, immutable generations, selective compaction, offline verification, and backup/restore.
Bounded asynchronous writer infrastructure with worker-service protocol, restart supervision, backpressure, request acknowledgment, and configurable queue limits.
Transactional request ledger with content digests, replay reconciliation, and retained-request idempotency across worker failures.
Fair multi-tenant writer admission with per-tenant accounting, starvation prevention, expiring claims, and bounded reservation capacity.
Configurable query execution budgets for joins, aggregates, sorting, and retained result rows, plus streaming result cursors for eligible queries.
Experimental segment-and-offset cold addressing and two-level page directories with bounded leaf caching for very large datasets.
Storage abstraction layer, in-memory filesystem, deterministic fault-injection laboratory, and simulated crash, power-loss, torn-write, and disk-full testing.
Persistent format registry, golden compatibility fixtures, corruption fuzzing, and deterministic benchmark laboratory with workload fingerprints and correctness oracles.
Storage amplification instrumentation, compaction planning, reader generation pins, and expanded operational diagnostics.
changed: Strengthened WAL recovery with committed-length witnesses, atomic witness creation, corruption detection, and conservative handling of ambiguous or damaged frames.
Hardened durable publication, manifest replacement, directory synchronization, and recovery after interrupted storage operations.
Improved writer correctness with typed commit acknowledgments, protected ledger tables, tenant-scoped request identities, and bounded supervisor bookkeeping.
Introduced byte-aware writer admission and more realistic heap accounting to reduce memory amplification under large or hostile requests.
Improved cold-storage scalability with streaming segment processing, packed page-directory metadata, and constant-time cache eviction.
Expanded query planning explanations and bounded execution behavior while preserving existing SQL semantics and storage compatibility.
Updated filesystem option types for Jess runtimes using l3i 2.11.0 or later, with expanded strict-check and regression coverage.
known_issues: Physical power-loss durability is not certified. Recovery assumes the underlying filesystem honors successful synchronization operations; lying or damaged storage can violate acknowledged-commit guarantees.
Windows and macOS durability and performance remain unqualified. The final hardening campaign was validated primarily on Linux.
The writer service uses an application-local transport without built-in authentication. Applications must enforce authorization, directory confinement, and exclusive ownership of ledger writes.
Request idempotency is guaranteed only while the corresponding ledger entries are retained. Pruning entries permits older request identifiers to be applied again.
Cold segment addressing and two-level page directories remain experimental and are not universally integrated into managed storage paths.
Resource limits bound specific queues, caches, and query operations; they do not impose a hard process-wide resident-memory ceiling.
Replication, distributed transactions, concurrent independent writers, and online backups are not implemented.
